The moon looks smooth in the night sky, but up close, it seems to have quite a lot of wrinkles. But there's no need for beauty serum. These wrinkles offer clues to how the moon shrank and to its surprising way of dressing. The team used camera images from the lunar probe LRO. They searched for cliffs on the moon's surface and marked them on a map. A wrinkle is a cliff with one steep side and one gentler side. These cliffs are thought to show where solid rock was squeezed together, with one side pushed up over the other. They're a record of a huge shoving match carved into the moon's surface. Using this map to work out how much the moon has shrunk, the team estimated that its radius had become about 42 to 46 meters smaller. By reading the wrinkles on its surface, scientists are investigating how a huge object in space has shrunk. Taking the moon's measurements is quite a detailed job.
